title: AI Unlocked: Finance & Accounting
blurb: For accountants, analysts, and finance teams: close-and-reporting acceleration, Excel/Sheets AI mastery, FP&A and analysis workflows, the finance-AI tool market compared, and the controls/audit-trail discipline regulators expect.

modules.d: Where AI creates value across the finance cycle — and why numbers demand stricter discipline than words.
modules.body:
Finance is a special case for AI

Language models are probabilistic: they predict plausible text. That is excellent for drafting, explaining and summarising, but dangerous for arithmetic and facts presented as certain. A sentence that is slightly wrong is a nuisance; a reconciliation that is slightly wrong can mislead a board, misstate tax or hide a fraud. Finance professionals who succeed with AI therefore adopt one governing principle: use AI to build, explain and check the work — let deterministic systems (spreadsheets, accounting software, code) do the calculation — and verify everything that leaves the team.

Mapping AI across the finance cycle

  • Transaction processing: extracting data from invoices and receipts, suggesting account codes, matching payments to invoices. Increasingly built into accounting platforms; still requires review of exceptions.
  • Record-to-report and month-end close: drafting reconciliation checklists, investigating variances, writing journal descriptions, and preparing close commentary.
  • Spreadsheets and analysis: writing and explaining formulas, cleaning data, building pivot tables and models faster.
  • FP&A: driver-based forecasts, scenario analysis, and the narrative explaining performance.
  • Reporting: management packs, board commentary, and summaries tailored to different audiences.
  • Audit and controls: testing populations of transactions for anomalies, documenting controls, and drafting policies.
  • Tax and compliance: summarising regulations and preparing questions for advisers — but tax positions require qualified review and authoritative sources.
The calculation boundary. Ask AI "Write an Excel formula that calculates the variance between actual and budget for each cost centre" — not "What is the variance between these numbers?". The first produces a transparent, auditable formula in a deterministic tool; the second produces an answer you must re-check by hand.

The changing role of finance professionals

As routine processing is automated, finance teams spend relatively more time on analysis, business partnering, controls and judgement. The skills that grow in value: understanding the business drivers behind numbers, communicating insight to non-finance leaders, designing controls for automated processes, and evaluating whether AI-produced work is right. A finance professional who cannot explain why a number moved is more exposed than one who cannot type a formula.

Risks specific to finance

  • Calculation errors presented confidently, especially with long tables pasted into chat tools.
  • Confidentiality: unpublished results, payroll, client financial data and price-sensitive information entered into tools without appropriate data protection — potentially a breach of law, contract or market rules.
  • Outdated or wrong rules: AI may describe accounting standards or tax rates incorrectly or from an earlier version.
  • Weakened audit trail: numbers that cannot be traced to source data and logic fail audit.
  • Automation bias: reviewers approving AI-prepared work too quickly because it looks professional.

A maturity view

Finance teams typically move from ad hoc individual use, to standardised prompts and templates with review rules, to embedded AI features in accounting and FP&A systems with documented controls, to optimised processes where close cycles, forecasting and reporting are redesigned around automation. Each step requires stronger controls, not weaker ones.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a finance transformation advisor. Ask me about my role, team size, accounting software, close timeline and biggest time sinks. Map AI opportunities across our finance cycle, rate each for value and risk, and recommend three starting use cases. For each, specify where the calculation must happen in a deterministic tool and what review control is required.

📚 Glossary

  • Deterministic tool: software that gives the same exact result from the same inputs, e.g. a spreadsheet formula
  • Record-to-report: the process from recording transactions to producing financial statements
  • FP&A: financial planning and analysis
  • Automation bias: over-trusting automated outputs
  • Audit trail: traceable path from reported figures back to source data and logic

📖 References

  • ICAEW — Generative AI guidance for accountants.
  • ACCA — Reports on AI and the accountancy profession.
  • IFAC — Technology and the future of the profession resources.

quiz.q: A finance analyst pastes 400 rows of transactions into a chat assistant and asks for the total by department. The assistant gives totals. What is the BEST practice?
opts: Ask the assistant for a pivot table or SUMIFS formula and calculate in the spreadsheet, then reconcile to the ledger
Round the totals to reduce error
Ask the assistant to double-check its own totals
Use the totals since the assistant is reliable at arithmetic
quiz.x: Calculations belong in deterministic tools with transparent logic; AI helps build the formula.

quiz.q: Which use of AI in finance carries the LOWEST risk?
opts: Drafting a plain-language explanation of a variance the analyst has already calculated and verified
Entering unpublished quarterly results into a free public chatbot
quiz.x: Explaining verified numbers is low risk; calculating tax, exposing confidential data and approving entries are high risk.

quiz.q: A manager approves an AI-prepared management pack without checking the figures because 'it looks very professional'. Which risk is this?
quiz.x: Polished output invites over-trust; review must be based on evidence, not appearance.

quiz.q: An AI assistant states a VAT rate for Cameroon. What should the accountant do before using it?
opts: Use it only for internal reports
Average it with last year's rate
Verify it against the current official source or tax adviser
Use it, since AI is trained on recent data
quiz.x: Rates and rules change; authoritative sources govern compliance.

quiz.q: Which skill becomes MORE valuable for finance professionals as AI automates processing?
opts: Explaining the business drivers behind the numbers and evaluating whether outputs are right
quiz.x: Judgement, business understanding and communication grow in value.

quiz.q: A CFO wants to paste draft annual results into a consumer AI tool before public release to write the press summary. What is the MAIN concern?
opts: Results must be in a specific format
The summary will be too long
Confidential, possibly price-sensitive information may be exposed without appropriate protection
quiz.x: Unpublished results may be confidential or market-sensitive; only approved tools with proper data terms should be used.

quiz.q: Auditors cannot trace a forecast figure back to its source data or logic because it was 'produced by the AI'. Which risk materialised?
quiz.x: Reported figures must be traceable to source and method.

quiz.q: A finance team moves from individual AI use to standard prompts, templates and documented review rules. Which maturity stage is this?
quiz.x: Standardisation creates consistent, governed practice before deeper system integration.

quiz.q: Which prompt BEST respects the calculation boundary?
opts: Tell me which products are most profitable
What is the gross margin for each product in this table?
Write a formula in column F that calculates gross margin % from revenue in C and cost of sales in D, handling zero revenue
Estimate gross margin for each product
quiz.x: Asking for a formula keeps calculation in the spreadsheet and makes logic auditable.

quiz.q: As AI features are embedded into accounting systems, what should happen to controls?
opts: Controls can be reduced because systems are smarter
Controls must be documented and strengthened for the automated processes
Controls become the IT department's sole responsibility
Controls are needed only at year-end
quiz.x: Automation shifts risk; controls must be redesigned and documented, not relaxed.

modules.d: Formulas, data cleaning, modelling and verification in Excel and Google Sheets — with AI as your expert pair.
modules.body:
The spreadsheet remains the finance professional's main instrument

Despite enterprise systems, most analysis, reconciliation and modelling still happens in Excel or Google Sheets. AI dramatically accelerates spreadsheet work: writing formulas you would otherwise search for, explaining inherited models, cleaning messy exports and building structures. The professional's job is to specify precisely and test rigorously.

Prompting for formulas

A good formula prompt states: the spreadsheet application and version (Excel 365 and Google Sheets differ), the sheet and column layout with sample values, the exact logic required, edge cases (blanks, zeros, errors, duplicates), and the output location. Example: "In Excel 365, Sheet 'Sales' has Date in A, Region in B, Product in C, Amount in D (rows 2–5000). On Sheet 'Summary', B1 is a region and B2 a month (first day of month). Write a formula returning total Amount for that region and month, returning 0 if none." A correct answer would use SUMIFS with date bounds such as EOMONTH.

The functions every finance user should command

  • Lookup: XLOOKUP (Excel 365 and Google Sheets) replaces VLOOKUP's fragility — it searches any direction and handles not-found values. INDEX/MATCH remains essential for older files.
  • Conditional aggregation: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS.
  • Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE — producing ranges that update automatically.
  • Readability: LET names intermediate calculations inside a formula; LAMBDA creates reusable custom functions in Excel.
  • Error handling: IFERROR and IFNA — use carefully; hiding all errors can conceal real problems.
  • Dates: EOMONTH, EDATE, NETWORKDAYS, YEARFRAC.

Cleaning data with AI help

Exports from banks, payroll and ERPs arrive with inconsistent dates, text-numbers, trailing spaces, merged headers and duplicates. AI can write formulas (TRIM, VALUE, TEXTSPLIT, DATEVALUE) or step-by-step Power Query transformations, which are repeatable every month — far better than manual cleaning. For recurring imports, ask AI to design the Power Query steps once and refresh monthly.

Test every formula like an auditor. ① Check it against three to five rows you calculate by hand, including an edge case. ② Reconcile totals to a control figure (the ledger, bank statement or source total). ③ Use Excel's Evaluate Formula or trace precedents to follow the logic. ④ Ask the AI to explain the formula line by line — if the explanation does not match your intent, the formula is wrong.

Understanding inherited models

Finance teams inherit complex workbooks with hard-coded numbers and undocumented logic. Paste a formula (not confidential data) and ask AI to explain it in plain language and identify risks: hard-coded constants, inconsistent ranges, circular references, or lookups that will break if rows are added. This turns days of reverse-engineering into hours.

Modelling standards

Good financial models separate inputs (clearly marked assumptions), calculations and outputs; avoid hard-coded numbers inside formulas; use consistent formulas across rows; include checks (balance sheet balances, totals reconcile) that flag errors visibly; and document sources. AI can audit a model structure against these standards and draft a model documentation sheet.

Built-in spreadsheet AI

Microsoft Copilot in Excel and Gemini in Google Sheets can analyse tables, suggest formulas, create charts and summarise data within the file. Availability and capabilities vary by licence and change frequently. Use them for speed, but apply the same tests: built-in does not mean verified.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my spreadsheet expert. I will describe my sheet layout with sample (non-confidential) values and the result I need. Write the formula for my exact application (Excel 365 or Google Sheets), explain it line by line, list edge cases it handles and does not handle, and give me three test rows with expected results. If a repeatable cleaning task is involved, propose Power Query steps instead.

📚 Glossary

  • XLOOKUP: flexible lookup function replacing VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP
  • SUMIFS: sums values meeting multiple criteria
  • Dynamic array: formula returning a range that resizes automatically
  • LET / LAMBDA: naming intermediate values / creating custom functions
  • Power Query: repeatable data import and transformation tool
  • Control figure: an independent total used to reconcile results

📖 References

  • Microsoft Support — Excel function reference and Copilot in Excel.
  • Google — Google Sheets function list and Gemini in Sheets.
  • ICAEW — Financial Modelling Code.
  • FAST Standard — financial modelling guidelines.

quiz.q: An AI-written SUMIFS formula returns a total that differs from the general ledger by 2,350. What should the analyst do FIRST?
opts: Ask the AI to regenerate the formula until it matches
Use the ledger figure and ignore the formula
Adjust the formula until it matches the ledger
Investigate the difference — test sample rows, check criteria ranges, date bounds and source completeness
quiz.x: Reconciliation differences must be understood, not forced. Testing rows and logic identifies the cause.

quiz.q: Which prompt is MOST likely to produce a correct formula?
opts: In Excel 365, Sales!A:D has Date, Region, Product, Amount. Summary!B1 is a region, B2 a month start. Return total Amount for that region and month; return 0 if none
Give me a formula for sales by region
How do I do sales totals in Excel?
quiz.x: Specifying application, layout, logic and edge cases produces accurate formulas.

quiz.q: An analyst wraps every formula in IFERROR(…, 0). What is the MAIN risk?
opts: Genuine errors, such as missing lookup values, are hidden as zeros
quiz.x: Blanket error suppression conceals real problems; handle specific, expected errors deliberately.

quiz.q: The same bank export must be cleaned every month. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Have a junior staff member clean it
Use AI to design Power Query steps once and refresh monthly
Ask AI to clean the pasted data in chat each month
quiz.x: Repeatable transformations reduce error and time and are auditable.

quiz.q: A VLOOKUP returns wrong values after a column is inserted in the lookup table. Which function would MOST reduce this risk?
quiz.x: XLOOKUP references return columns directly rather than by column number, so inserted columns do not break it.

quiz.q: Which practice BEST verifies an AI-written formula?
opts: Hand-calculating several rows including an edge case and reconciling totals to a control figure
Checking that it returns a number
Comparing it with a colleague's formula
Asking the AI whether it is correct
quiz.x: Independent testing and reconciliation provide evidence of correctness.

quiz.q: A model has '*1.18' typed inside dozens of formulas for a tax rate. What modelling standard does this violate?
opts: Separating inputs from calculations — assumptions should be in clearly marked input cells
quiz.x: Hard-coded constants hide assumptions and make updates error-prone.

quiz.q: An analyst inherits a workbook with a complex nested formula. What is the BEST use of AI?
opts: Replace the formula with a new one without understanding it
Ask AI to explain the formula in plain language and identify risks such as hard-codes and fragile ranges
Paste the whole confidential workbook into a public chatbot
quiz.x: Explaining logic and risks accelerates understanding while keeping confidential data protected.

quiz.q: Copilot in Excel suggests a formula for a key board figure. How should it be treated?
opts: As verified, since it is built into Excel
With the same testing and reconciliation as any other formula
As acceptable for internal use only
quiz.x: Built-in tools are faster, not automatically correct.

quiz.q: Which function would MOST appropriately return all invoices over 1,000,000 FCFA for a selected supplier as a live list?
quiz.x: FILTER returns a dynamic range of rows meeting criteria.

modules.t: Tool Study: The Finance AI Market
modules.d: Evaluating AI tools for finance by control, accuracy, integration and data protection.
modules.body:
A fast-moving market — evaluate by criteria

Finance AI tools evolve rapidly, and vendors' claims frequently outrun reality. Rather than memorising products, finance leaders need a robust evaluation method. Always confirm current features, pricing, regional availability and data terms with the vendor and through a controlled trial.

Tool categories

  • General AI assistants (for example ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot): drafting, explaining, formula help, policy summaries, analysis of documents. Business plans typically offer stronger data protections than consumer plans.
  • Spreadsheet-embedded AI: Copilot in Excel, Gemini in Google Sheets — analysis and formula assistance inside the file.
  • Accounting platforms with AI features: cloud accounting systems (for example QuickBooks, Xero, Sage, Zoho Books) increasingly offer automatic categorisation, bank-matching suggestions and invoice capture.
  • ERP-embedded AI: large systems (for example SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics) add AI for anomaly detection, forecasting and assistants.
  • Accounts payable and expense automation: invoice capture, three-way matching, approval routing and expense audit.
  • Close management and reconciliation: task tracking, automated matching and variance flagging during month-end.
  • FP&A platforms: planning, forecasting and scenario tools with AI-assisted forecasting and narrative.
  • Audit analytics: full-population testing of transactions for anomalies and unusual patterns.
Local fit matters. For organisations in OHADA member states such as Cameroon, check whether a tool supports the SYSCOHADA chart of accounts and reporting formats, local currency (XAF), French-language interfaces, and local tax requirements — or whether costly customisation would be needed. Many tools built for US or European markets do not do this out of the box.

Evaluation criteria for finance tools

  1. Accuracy: test on your real (anonymised where needed) data — measure error rates, not demo quality.
  2. Control and auditability: are AI suggestions logged? Can you see who approved what? Can outputs be traced to source?
  3. Data protection and residency: where is data stored and processed, is it used to train models, what certifications (such as ISO 27001, SOC 2) does the vendor hold, and is a data-processing agreement available?
  4. Integration: does it connect to your accounting system, bank feeds and spreadsheets without manual exports?
  5. Local compliance: accounting framework (IFRS, SYSCOHADA), tax, e-invoicing and language.
  6. Segregation of duties support: can roles and approvals be configured?
  7. Total cost of ownership: licences, implementation, training, maintenance and change management.
  8. Vendor viability and support: local support, roadmap and exit options for your data.

Running a controlled pilot

Choose one process with measurable pain — for example invoice processing. Establish the baseline: volume, time per invoice, error rate, cycle time. Run the tool in parallel with the existing process for one month, comparing results line by line. Measure accuracy, time saved and exceptions. Only switch over when parallel running shows reliable results and controls are documented. This protects the books from a failed implementation.

Build, buy or configure

Many finance teams can achieve significant gains by configuring what they already own — enabling AI features in existing software, building Power Query and template workflows, and using an approved general assistant — before buying new platforms. Buy when volume, complexity or control requirements justify it. Build custom solutions only with proper IT governance.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my finance systems selection advisor. Ask me about our accounting framework (IFRS or SYSCOHADA), software, transaction volumes, currency, language and pain points. Recommend tool categories to evaluate, build a weighted scoring matrix using the eight criteria in this module, and design a one-month parallel-run pilot with baseline and success measures. List the questions I must ask vendors about data protection and auditability.

📚 Glossary

  • SYSCOHADA: the OHADA accounting system used in member states including Cameroon
  • Data residency: where data is stored and processed geographically
  • Parallel run: operating new and old processes side by side to compare results
  • Three-way match: matching purchase order, goods receipt and invoice before payment
  • SOC 2 / ISO 27001: common information-security assurance standards

📖 References

  • OHADA — Uniform Act on Accounting Law and Financial Reporting (SYSCOHADA revised).
  • IFRS Foundation — IFRS Accounting Standards.
  • AICPA — SOC 2 reports; ISO/IEC 27001.
  • Gartner and vendor documentation — verify current product capabilities.

quiz.q: A vendor demo shows 99% accuracy in invoice capture. What is the BEST next step?
opts: Purchase, since the demo was convincing
Test the tool on your own representative invoices and measure error rates
Ask the vendor for references only
quiz.x: Demo data is curated; real accuracy must be measured on your documents.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian company evaluates a US-built accounting tool. Which question is MOST critical?
opts: Does it support SYSCOHADA, XAF, French and local tax requirements without costly customisation?
Does it have a mobile app?
Does it have a modern interface?
Is it popular in the US?
quiz.x: Local framework, currency, language and tax compliance determine fit.

quiz.q: Which criterion MOST directly supports external audit?
opts: Control and auditability — logged suggestions, approvals and traceability
quiz.x: Auditors need traceable evidence of who did what and how figures were produced.

quiz.q: A finance team wants to replace its invoice process with an AI tool immediately at month-end. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Use the tool for half the invoices without comparison
Switch over immediately to save time
Run the new tool in parallel with the existing process and compare results before switching
quiz.x: Parallel running proves reliability before the books depend on the new process.

quiz.q: Before uploading supplier invoices to an AI tool, which vendor question is MOST important for data protection?
opts: How many customers do you have?
Where is our data stored and processed, is it used for training, and can we sign a data-processing agreement?
quiz.x: Data location, use and contractual protection determine compliance.

quiz.q: A small finance team has Microsoft 365 and a cloud accounting system with unused AI features. What is the MOST sensible first step?
opts: Configure existing AI features and templates before buying new tools
Wait for the market to mature
quiz.x: Configuring what you own often delivers fast value with lower risk and cost.

quiz.q: Which pilot baseline measure is MOST useful for invoice automation?
opts: Staff opinions of the old process
Volume, time per invoice, error rate and cycle time before the pilot
quiz.x: Quantitative baselines allow objective comparison.

quiz.q: An AP tool lets the same user capture, approve and pay invoices. Which control concern does this raise?
quiz.x: Combining incompatible duties increases fraud and error risk; tools should support role separation.

quiz.q: Why should total cost of ownership include change management?
opts: Training and process redesign often cost as much as or more than licences and determine adoption
quiz.x: Adoption depends on people and process changes, which carry real cost.

quiz.q: A vendor holds a SOC 2 report. What does this primarily provide?
opts: Guarantee that AI outputs are accurate
Independent assurance about the vendor's security and related controls
quiz.x: SOC 2 addresses controls over security and related principles, not accounting accuracy or local compliance.

modules.d: Variance analysis, driver-based forecasting, scenarios and commentary that leaders actually use.
modules.body:
From numbers to decisions

Financial planning and analysis exists to help leaders make better decisions: where to invest, what to cut, how to price, and what risks lie ahead. The value is not in the spreadsheet but in the insight and how clearly it is communicated. AI accelerates the mechanics and drafting so analysts can spend more time understanding causes and advising.

Variance analysis that explains, not just reports

A variance tells you what changed; analysis tells you why. Break revenue and cost variances into drivers. For sales: price variance = (actual price − budget price) × actual quantity; volume variance = (actual quantity − budget quantity) × budget price. Together they reconcile to the total revenue variance. Similar logic applies to costs (rate and usage variances). Then investigate causes: a negative volume variance might come from a lost client, delayed product launch or seasonal shift. Good commentary states the variance, the driver, the cause, whether it is timing or permanent, and the action.

Worked example. Budget: 1,000 units at 5,000 FCFA = 5,000,000. Actual: 900 units at 5,400 FCFA = 4,860,000. Total variance −140,000. Price variance = (5,400 − 5,000) × 900 = +360,000 favourable. Volume variance = (900 − 1,000) × 5,000 = −500,000 adverse. Commentary: "Revenue was 140,000 FCFA below budget. An 8% price increase added 360,000, but volume fell 10%, costing 500,000, mainly due to the loss of Distributor X in May. We expect volume to recover partially from Q3 with two new distributors."

Driver-based forecasting

Instead of forecasting each line from last year plus a percentage, driver-based models link outcomes to operational drivers: number of customers × average order value × purchase frequency; headcount × average cost; units produced × cost per unit. Changing a driver updates the forecast consistently. AI can help identify plausible drivers, structure the model and write formulas — while finance and operations agree the assumptions.

Rolling forecasts and scenarios

A rolling forecast always looks a fixed period ahead (for example 12 or 18 months), updated monthly or quarterly, rather than stopping at year-end. Scenario analysis tests base, upside and downside cases with explicitly different assumptions — for example a currency movement, a loss of a major customer or a fuel price rise. Sensitivity analysis changes one variable at a time to show which assumptions matter most. AI is useful for generating a structured list of plausible scenarios and drafting the narrative of their implications, but the quantification must be in the model.

Key ratios and what they reveal

  • Profitability: gross margin, operating margin, net margin, return on capital.
  • Liquidity: current ratio, quick ratio, cash conversion cycle (DSO + DIO − DPO).
  • Efficiency: asset turnover, inventory days, receivable days.
  • Leverage: debt-to-equity, interest cover.

Ratios are meaningful only in context — trends over time, comparison with budget and with peers — and alongside understanding of the business.

Writing commentary leaders use

Executives want the answer first. Structure commentary as: headline (the key message), the two or three most important drivers, risks and opportunities ahead, and recommended actions or decisions needed. Avoid listing every variance; focus on what is material. AI can draft commentary from your verified analysis, adapt it for different audiences — board, operations managers, donors, lenders — and check clarity. You remain responsible for every number and claim.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my FP&A partner. I will give you budget and actual figures for price, volume and costs (non-confidential or anonymised). Build the formulas to split the variance into price and volume (and rate and usage for costs), check that they reconcile, and draft a one-paragraph management commentary leading with the headline. Then propose base, upside and downside scenarios with the key assumptions to model, and identify the two most sensitive drivers.

📚 Glossary

  • Price / volume variance: splitting revenue variance into price and quantity effects
  • Driver-based forecast: forecast built from operational drivers
  • Rolling forecast: forecast that always extends a fixed period ahead
  • Sensitivity analysis: changing one assumption to see its effect
  • Cash conversion cycle: DSO + DIO − DPO

📖 References

  • CIMA — Management accounting and variance analysis resources.
  • AFP — FP&A guides and best practices.
  • Minto, B. The Pyramid Principle — for commentary structure.

quiz.q: Budget: 2,000 units at 3,000 FCFA. Actual: 2,200 units at 2,800 FCFA. What is the volume variance?
Using the same data, what is the price variance?
Which commentary BEST serves a CEO?
opts: A list of every account with its variance
The full trial balance with notes
Headline result, two or three key drivers with causes, outlook, and recommended actions
A detailed explanation of the forecasting method
quiz.x: Leaders need the answer first, focused on material drivers and decisions.

quiz.q: A company forecasts each cost line as 'last year plus 5%'. What is the MAIN weakness compared with driver-based forecasting?
opts: It cannot be done in Excel
It does not link costs to the operational drivers that actually change them
quiz.x: Driver-based models connect outcomes to activity, so changes in operations update the forecast consistently.

quiz.q: A rolling forecast differs from an annual budget mainly because it:
opts: Is prepared only once per year
Always extends a fixed period ahead and is updated regularly
quiz.x: Rolling forecasts maintain a constant horizon, improving forward visibility.

quiz.q: An analyst asks AI to 'estimate the profit impact of a 15% depreciation of the local currency'. What is the BEST approach?
opts: Use AI to identify affected lines and assumptions, then quantify the scenario in the model
Ask several AI tools and average their answers
Use the AI's estimate in the board pack
quiz.x: AI structures the scenario; the model quantifies it transparently.

quiz.q: DSO = 60 days, DIO = 45 days, DPO = 30 days. What is the cash conversion cycle?
Revenue fell short of budget, but the variance is entirely because a large order shipped on 2 July instead of 28 June. How should commentary treat it?
opts: As a permanent loss of revenue
As a timing variance expected to reverse next month
quiz.x: Distinguishing timing from permanent variances is essential for decisions.

quiz.q: Which analysis BEST shows which assumption a forecast is most sensitive to?
opts: Sensitivity analysis changing one variable at a time
quiz.x: Sensitivity analysis reveals which assumptions most affect results.

quiz.q: AI drafts board commentary that states 'margin improved due to stronger supplier negotiations'. The analyst has no evidence for this cause. What should happen?
opts: Remove or verify the cause with the procurement team before submission
Keep it, since it sounds plausible
Keep it but add a footnote
quiz.x: Causes in commentary must be evidenced; plausible AI explanations are not facts.

modules.d: Keeping AI-assisted finance reliable, auditable and compliant with IFRS, SYSCOHADA and internal control frameworks.
modules.body:
Why controls matter more, not less, with AI

Internal controls exist to provide reasonable assurance that financial reporting is reliable, operations effective and laws respected. AI changes how work is done — and therefore where errors and fraud can occur. A team that adopts AI without redesigning controls is quietly increasing its risk.

The COSO internal control framework

The COSO framework, widely used worldwide, has five components: control environment (tone at the top, integrity, accountability), risk assessment (identifying risks to objectives, including fraud and change risks), control activities (approvals, reconciliations, segregation of duties, system controls), information and communication (quality information flowing to the right people), and monitoring activities (ongoing and periodic evaluation). Introducing AI should trigger a risk assessment: what new risks does this process change create, and which controls address them?

Key controls for AI-assisted finance

  • Maker–checker review: AI-assisted work (journals, reconciliations, reports) is prepared by one person and reviewed by another with evidence of review.
  • Segregation of duties: no single person (or automated workflow they control) can initiate, approve and record a transaction.
  • Reconciliation to independent sources: AI-produced figures reconcile to the ledger, bank statements or sub-ledgers.
  • Logging and documentation: prompts, tool versions, inputs and outputs for significant processes are retained where practical; methods are documented.
  • Access controls: only authorised staff use approved tools with financial data; data rules define what may be entered.
  • Change management: changes to automated workflows, models or AI configurations are approved, tested and recorded.
  • Exception handling: automated processes route unusual items to human review rather than processing them silently.
Model risk. Any model used for decisions — a forecast, an expected credit loss model, an AI classifier for expenses — can be wrong. Model risk management means documenting the model's purpose, assumptions and limitations, validating it independently, monitoring performance over time, and having a human owner accountable for it.

Accounting frameworks and AI

AI can summarise and explain standards, but accounting judgements must rely on the authoritative text and qualified professionals. In OHADA member states such as Cameroon, entities apply the SYSCOHADA system under the OHADA Uniform Act on accounting (revised version in force since 2018), with IFRS required for certain entities such as those listed or issuing public securities. Elsewhere, IFRS or national standards apply. An AI answer about revenue recognition, leases or provisions is a starting point for research, never the final authority. Always cite the specific standard and paragraph in working papers.

Confidentiality and data protection

Finance handles payroll, customer financial data, banking details and unpublished results. Apply clear rules: personal and confidential financial data only in approved tools with appropriate contractual protections; no unpublished price-sensitive information in public tools; anonymise where analysis does not require identities. Comply with applicable data protection law and professional confidentiality duties.

Fraud and AI

AI cuts both ways. It helps detect fraud through full-population analytics — duplicate payments, round-amount patterns, unusual timing, vendors sharing bank details with employees. But criminals also use AI: convincing phishing emails, fake invoices and voice or video impersonation of executives requesting urgent transfers. Controls must include independent verification of payment instructions through a known channel, especially for changes to supplier bank details and urgent requests from "senior executives".

Professional ethics

Professional bodies' codes — such as the IESBA Code of Ethics — require integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour. Using AI does not reduce these duties: the professional remains responsible for the work signed.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my internal control advisor. I will describe a finance process where we use or plan to use AI. Map the process steps, identify the new risks AI introduces, and map controls to the five COSO components. Recommend specific maker-checker, segregation, reconciliation, logging and exception-handling controls, and draft a short control description suitable for audit documentation.

📚 Glossary

  • COSO: framework of five internal control components
  • Maker–checker: preparation by one person, review by another
  • Segregation of duties: separating initiation, approval, recording and custody
  • Model risk: risk of loss from incorrect or misused models
  • Business email compromise: fraud using impersonated emails to divert payments

📖 References

  • COSO (2013). Internal Control — Integrated Framework.
  • OHADA — Uniform Act on Accounting Law and Financial Reporting (revised 2017, applicable from 2018).
  • IFRS Foundation — IFRS Accounting Standards.
  • IESBA — International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants.
  • ACFE — Fraud examination resources.

quiz.q: An automated workflow lets an accountant generate AI-suggested journal entries and post them directly without review. Which control is MOST lacking?
quiz.x: Entries require independent review with evidence before posting.

quiz.q: Introducing an AI expense-classification tool should trigger which COSO activity FIRST?
opts: A risk assessment of the changed process
quiz.x: Process changes create new risks that must be assessed before designing controls.

quiz.q: A supplier emails new bank details with an urgent payment request 'from the CEO'. The email looks genuine. What should the finance team do?
opts: Reply to the email asking for confirmation
Verify the change and request independently through a known channel before paying
Ask AI whether the email looks genuine
Pay promptly to avoid offending the CEO
quiz.x: Independent verification through known contact details defeats impersonation; replying to the email does not.

quiz.q: An AI model classifies expenses with 96% accuracy. Who should be accountable for its performance?
opts: A named human model owner within the organisation
quiz.x: Model risk management requires a human owner who monitors performance and limitations.

quiz.q: An accountant asks AI how to account for a complex lease and records the treatment based on the answer. What is missing?
opts: Verification against the authoritative standard and, where needed, qualified professional review
quiz.x: Standards' authoritative text and professional judgement govern accounting treatment.

quiz.q: Which entity in Cameroon would MOST likely be required to apply IFRS in addition to or instead of SYSCOHADA?
opts: An entity whose securities are publicly traded
quiz.x: Under OHADA rules, IFRS applies to certain entities such as listed or public-issuer companies; most others apply SYSCOHADA.

quiz.q: Which control BEST addresses AI processing unusual transactions silently?
opts: Exception handling that routes unusual items to human review
quiz.x: Exceptions must surface for human judgement.

quiz.q: An analytics test finds an employee's home bank account matches a supplier's bank details. What is this an example of?
opts: Full-population fraud analytics detecting a red flag
quiz.x: Data matching across populations can reveal potential fraud for investigation.

quiz.q: A team changes the prompt and settings of an automated reconciliation workflow without testing or approval. Which control is violated?
quiz.x: Changes to automated processes need approval, testing and documentation.

quiz.q: Under professional ethics codes, who is responsible for the accuracy of AI-assisted work an accountant signs?
opts: The professional accountant who signs it
quiz.x: Professional responsibility remains with the accountant.

modules.t: Capstone: Your Finance AI Workflow File
modules.d: Design, document and test one AI-assisted finance workflow to audit-ready standard.
modules.body:
The goal: one workflow, done properly

Rather than collecting tips, you will redesign one real finance workflow from your own work using AI — and document it so that a colleague can run it and an auditor can rely on it. Typical choices: monthly variance commentary, bank reconciliation preparation, supplier invoice coding, cash flow forecast update, expense review, or a management pack.

The workflow file structure

  1. Process overview: purpose, frequency, owner, inputs, outputs and users of the output.
  2. Before-and-after map: the current steps with time per step, and the redesigned steps showing where AI is used.
  3. Calculation boundary: which steps use deterministic tools (formulas, Power Query, accounting system) and which use AI for drafting, explanation or checking.
  4. Prompt library: the exact prompts used, with input templates and expected output format.
  5. Data rules: what data is used, classification, the approved tool and anonymisation steps.
  6. Controls: maker–checker review, reconciliations to control figures, exception handling, and evidence retained.
  7. Testing record: results of at least one parallel run comparing the new workflow with the old.
  8. Benefits measurement: time saved, error rate, cycle time, and quality feedback from users.
  9. Risks and limitations: what could go wrong and how it is mitigated.
  10. Maintenance: who updates the workflow and when it is reviewed.
The colleague test. Give your workflow file to a colleague who has never done the process. If they can produce the correct output, with the same controls, using only the file, your documentation is good enough. If they need to ask you questions, improve the file.

Measuring and presenting the benefit

Quantify the baseline and new performance. For example: "Monthly variance commentary previously took 9 hours over 3 days; the redesigned workflow takes 3.5 hours in 1 day, with commentary rated clearer by the management team, and no reconciliation errors in two parallel runs." Translate time saved into value: what higher-value work will the team do with the freed time?

Scaling responsibly

Once one workflow is proven, use the same file structure for the next. A finance team that builds five well-documented workflows over a year has transformed its operations with controls intact — far more valuable than widespread, undocumented use.

Your capstone deliverable

Submit the completed workflow file, the evidence from one parallel run, and a one-page summary for your finance leader with the benefits, controls and recommendation. Your mentor reviews it for accuracy, control quality and practicality.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my finance workflow designer. I will describe one recurring finance process. Help me build the full workflow file: process overview, before-and-after map with time estimates, calculation boundary, exact prompts with input templates, data classification, controls with evidence, a parallel-run test plan, benefit measures, risks and maintenance. Then review the file as an external auditor and list any gaps.

📚 Glossary

  • Workflow file: complete documentation of a redesigned process
  • Parallel run: running old and new processes side by side to compare
  • Colleague test: checking that someone else can run the process from the documentation
  • Control figure: independent total used to verify output

📖 References

  • COSO (2013). Internal Control — Integrated Framework.
  • ICAEW — Generative AI guidance.
  • Team21 Academy, AI Unlocked workflow templates.

quiz.q: Which choice of capstone workflow is MOST appropriate?
opts: Redesigning the monthly variance commentary process with documented prompts, controls and testing
quiz.x: One real, recurring process redesigned and documented produces measurable, auditable value.

quiz.q: In the workflow file, which step belongs in a deterministic tool rather than AI?
opts: Improving the clarity of a paragraph
quiz.x: Calculations belong in spreadsheets or systems; AI drafts and explains.

quiz.q: A colleague cannot complete the process from the workflow file without asking several questions. What should happen?
opts: Improve the documentation until the colleague can complete it independently
Assign the process only to the author
quiz.x: The colleague test reveals documentation gaps.

quiz.q: Why does the file include a parallel-run testing record?
opts: To provide evidence that the new workflow produces correct results before relying on it
quiz.x: Evidence of comparison builds confidence for management and auditors.

quiz.q: Which benefit statement is MOST credible?
opts: AI made the process much better
The team loves the new tool
Commentary time fell from 9 to 3.5 hours with no reconciliation errors in two parallel runs
quiz.x: Quantified, evidenced benefits are credible.

quiz.q: Which section of the workflow file shows what data may be entered into which tool?
quiz.x: Data rules define classification, approved tools and anonymisation.

quiz.q: After proving one workflow, what does the course recommend?
opts: Allow unrestricted use of AI everywhere
Apply the same file structure to the next workflow, building a set of documented processes
quiz.x: Scaling with the same standard preserves control while increasing value.

quiz.q: Which control evidence is MOST valuable to retain for an audited process?
opts: The reviewer's sign-off and reconciliation to the control figure
Screenshots of the AI interface design
quiz.x: Evidence of review and reconciliation demonstrates the control operated.

quiz.q: Who should be named in the maintenance section?
opts: A responsible owner who updates and reviews the workflow on a schedule
quiz.x: Ongoing ownership keeps the workflow accurate as tools and processes change.

quiz.q: The redesigned workflow saves time but introduces a new risk of confidential payroll data entering a general tool. What should the file include?
opts: A mitigation such as anonymisation or use of an approved protected tool, documented in risks and data rules
A recommendation to stop the workflow
quiz.x: Risks must be identified and mitigated with specific controls.
